provenance: Lane split authored by the Stage-2 decision-agent (read-only; returns JSON in reply) and persisted by the orchestrator as the agent's returned detect-vs-hunt partition. Detection = seed complement of the agent's hunt set; validated to cover the Stage-1 seed exactly with no overlap/dup, and det-count reconciled against the agent's summary. All ids verified present in the CI's bundled ATT&CK dataset. Per-technique rationale shows the Stage-1 detection-feasibility basis.

detection_candidates.rationale: high — execution of Mimikatz/ProcDump/WCE and process access to credential stores is highly observable in EDR and process-access telemetry
high — process access to lsass.exe (handle open, ProcDump -ma lsass) and Mimikatz signatures are strong, well-covered detections
medium — bulk local file collection is common; suspicious mainly via staging/archiving lineage and access to unusual document stores
medium — reg query is common; value comes from watching sensitive keys in a recon-burst/process-lineage context
medium — remote-host enumeration (nbtscan/ping sweeps) is detectable via connection-fanout analytics and known-tool execution signatures
medium — RDP lateral movement is detectable via 4624 type-10 logons, internal-RDP fanout, and impossible-travel analytics; a strong detection surface given APT39's reliance on valid-account RDP
high — SMB admin-share access and PsExec service creation (7045/5145) are strongly detectable in Windows and network telemetry
medium — SSH client execution and outbound SSH from unusual hosts are detectable via process + network telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — packed binaries are detectable via entropy/section anomalies and packer signatures but require dedicated static scanning

detection_candidates.technique_name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Encrypted/Encoded File
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — high-entropy/encoded files are detectable via file-entropy analytics but require dedicated scanning
medium — whoami is common; value is in process-lineage correlation (spawned by script host / web shell)

detection_candidates.technique_name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — legit-looking names in non-standard paths are detectable via path/name baselining and signature-vs-name mismatch
medium — scanning bursts are detectable via network/connection-fanout analytics and known-tool signatures
high — scheduled-task creation is logged (Event ID 4698 / Task Scheduler operational) and highly detectable, especially with script/executable actions
medium — generic parent; value comes from specific interpreter sub-techniques with process-lineage context
high — script-block/module logging and suspicious PowerShell parenting are core, well-covered detections

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Visual Basic
detection_candidates.rationale: high — wscript/cscript executing VBS, especially spawned by Office, is a strong detectable signal
medium — python.exe execution in enterprise contexts is detectable via process telemetry and unusual interpreter presence on non-dev hosts

detection_candidates.technique_name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: AutoHotKey & AutoIT
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — AutoIt/AutoHotKey interpreter execution is detectable via process telemetry and is unusual in most enterprise baselines
medium — file deletion is detectable via file-system audit / EDR delete events but is noisy and needs correlation with prior payload writes
medium — HTTP(S) C2 is detectable via proxy/beacon analytics and URI/JA3 anomalies but blends with normal web traffic
medium — DNS-based C2 is detectable via query-length/entropy/volume analytics and NXDOMAIN patterns, but requires full DNS logging that is frequently under-instrumented
medium — local staging is common; suspicious when tied to archiving utilities writing large archives to temp/staging paths

medium — valid-account abuse is detectable via anomalous logon analytics (impossible travel, new host/time, first-seen device) but blends with legitimate use; a strong identity-monitoring detection surface for APT39
high — remote downloads via certutil/BITS and unexpected inbound file writes are strongly detectable in process + network telemetry
medium — brute force is detectable via authentication-failure spikes (4625) and lockout telemetry
medium — 'net view' / share enumeration is detectable via command-line logging in recon-burst context
high — local account creation is logged (Event ID 4720) and is a high-fidelity persistence detection
high — 'certutil -decode' and script-based decode routines are directly observable in command-line and script-block logging

medium — SQLi and public-app exploitation are detectable via WAF/web-server logs and anomalous DB-to-webserver process behavior; the SQLi-to-webshell chain is a signature APT39 pattern warranting targeted web-tier monitoring
medium — BITS jobs are detectable via BITS-Client operational logs and bitsadmin/PowerShell BITS cmdlet command-lines, but require targeted logging
medium — malicious-link clicks are detectable via email/URL-gateway and proxy logs; endpoint signal is indirect
high — Office apps spawning script/child processes after macro enablement is a core detectable behavior

high — web shells are detectable via web-server worker processes (w3wp.exe) spawning cmd/powershell, new/modified .aspx files in web roots, and anomalous IIS request patterns; ANTAK/ASPXSpy web-shell use is a signature APT39 tradecraft and a prime detection surface
high — modification of HKLM\...\Windows\AppInit_DLLs is a rare, high-fidelity registry-modification detection

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
detection_candidates.rationale: high — Run-key writes and Startup-folder drops are detectable via registry-modification and file-creation telemetry (Autoruns-class monitoring)

detection_candidates.technique_name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Shortcut Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — malicious .lnk creation/modification in startup/user paths is detectable via file-creation telemetry and shortcut-target analysis

detection_candidates.technique_name: Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing Policy Modification
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — signing-policy/DSE modifications (bcdedit testsigning, registry policy changes) are detectable via command-line and registry telemetry but require targeted rules
medium — credential-store access is detectable mainly via known-tool execution signatures and file/vault access telemetry

detection_candidates.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
detection_candidates.rationale: medium — archiving-utility execution producing large archives in staging paths is detectable via process + file-creation telemetry
medium — attachment-based spearphishing is detectable via mail sandboxing and macro-content analysis at the gateway
medium — link-based spearphishing is detectable via URL rewriting/detonation and proxy telemetry
high — service creation/execution (Event ID 7045 / 4697) is strongly detectable, especially with anomalous binary paths

hunting_candidates.rationale: low — exfil embedded in the C2 channel blends with beacon traffic; hunt on outbound volume anomalies and long-lived sessions
low — input-capture APIs leave little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — keystroke-hooking leaves little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — file/directory enumeration is ubiquitous; better as a hunt in tight recon-burst lineage context
low — internal proxy relays are subtle; hunt on unexpected host-to-host relay patterns and internal listeners
low — external proxy chains are off-victim; hunt on connections to known proxy/anonymization endpoints
low — legitimate-web-service C2 blends with sanctioned SaaS traffic; hunt on anomalous automation patterns to those services
low — screen-capture APIs leave little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — clipboard-capture leaves little discrete log signal; behavioral/EDR hunt candidate
low — tool acquisition itself is off-endpoint; downstream use is where detection lands — this entry is a hunt/intel candidate
